response.passage: Cells are the fundamental building blocks of all living things, and their size does not change based on the size of the organism. Whether it is a tiny bacterium or a massive elephant, cells remain microscopic. Inside every cell, the nucleus acts as a control center by storing genetic information, but it is not the only place where DNA is found. For instance, mitochondria also contain their own genetic material to help manage energy production. This energy is essential for all cells, including those in plants, which rely on mitochondria just as much as animal cells do. To maintain their internal environment, cells are enclosed by a flexible cell membrane that acts as a selective gatekeeper, allowing specific substances to enter and exit. Unlike the rigid cell wall found in plants, which provides structural support, the membrane is dynamic and permeable. Furthermore, even the simplest unicellular organisms perform all life processes, such as respiration and reproduction, proving they are just as alive as complex multicellular beings. Every part of the cell, from the organelles to the cytoplasm, is composed of atoms, which are the basic particles of matter found throughout the entire cell structure.
response.summary: Cells are the basic units of life that function independently regardless of an organism's size. They contain specialized structures like membranes and organelles that work together to sustain life processes.
